audit.reasoning: (1) Quote: confirmed verbatim at Nadzhip 1971:63 in the archive.org scanned text (now in custody under the audit dir); the record's top-level quote/cite/loc/grade fields are empty and should be populated from sources[0]. (2) Deciding source is a 1971 Nauka grammar sketch (~160 pp), impressionistic; StressTyp2 and Gordon 2002 code 'Final' from the same tradition. It is not the fullest description — Hahn 1991 (632-pp reference grammar, not held, print-only) reportedly gives a heavy-penult-else-final rule and the held Engesæth et al. 2010 handbook gives leftmost-closed-else-final — but the newest and only multi-speaker production study, McCollum 2020 (fetched sources now), finds stress fixed on the final syllable even after closed penults and calls Uyghur 'a language with fixed stress placement', and Hahn 1998 also says final. sources.citation: Mayer, Connor, Adam McCollum & Gülnar Eziz. 2022. Issues in Uyghur phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 16(12): e12478. doi:10.1111/lnc3.12478 (eScholarship qt1ch4r29j, CC BY-NC).
sources.quote: 'The status of phonemic vowel length and stress in Uyghur is somewhat unclear'; Yakup 2013 / Yakup & Sereno 2016 show stress reflected only in duration and 'Uyghur speakers frequently disagreed as to which syllables were stressed in many words'; Major & Mayer attribute pitch contours to phrasal prosody. Tentative synthesis: closed and stressed syllables heavy; 'Initial and final syllables are both stressed by default'; 'Certain roots are lexically specified for stress position'.

sources.citation: McCollum, Adam G. 2020. Sonority-driven stress and vowel reduction in Uyghur. Proceedings of the 2019 Annual Meeting on Phonology (AMP 8). doi:10.3765/amp.v8i0.4693 (12 pp; fetched sources via web.archive.org id_ capture of the LSA download link).
sources.quote: Lists prior descriptions: Nadzhip 1971:63-65 ultima; Hahn 1991:26-28 heavy penult else ultima; Hahn 1998:382 ultima; Engesæth et al. 2010:3-4 leftmost heavy else ultima. Production study (9 speakers): 'I contend that stress in Uyghur is final and weight-sensitive' (weight shows up as lengthening of stressed final high vowels, not as stress shift; tokens with closed penults such as bæl.ˈdin, sæl.ˈlæm, iʧ.ˈtin carry final stress); Conclusion: 'I have argued that stress is final in Uyghur ... Results from a production study support the finality of stress ... a language with fixed stress placement
sources.locator: p. 2-3 ex. (2) survey of descriptions; sec. 3-4 pp. 3-5 production data; sec. 7 Conclusion p. 11
sources.note: Only multi-speaker production study of stress placement; finds fixed final stress even after closed penults, i.e. instrumental support for our coding against Hahn 1991/Engesæth 2010 — should be cited as co-deciding evidence.

sources.citation: Major, Travis & Connor Mayer. 2018. Towards a phonological model of Uyghur intonation. Proc. Speech Prosody 2018, 744-748. doi:10.21437/SpeechProsody.2018-151 (ISCA archive, open).
sources.quote: Uyghur is 'a stress language that only uses edge-marking intonation'; replicates the Yakup & Sereno minimal stress pairs (Acha vs aCHA) in sentence-initial and medial position: duration, not f0, is the only correlate of stress; fn. 1: 'This tendency for final stress is robust across Turkic, but each language has developed a unique system.'

sources.citation: Yakup, Mahire & Joan A. Sereno. 2016. Acoustic correlates of lexical stress in Uyghur. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 46(1): 61-77. doi:10.1017/S0025100315000183 (author-lab copy, kuppl.ku.edu).
sources.quote: Earlier Chinese acoustic studies (Liang & Zhang 2008; Jiang et al. 2010) 'assumed that stress would fall on the final syllable'. Treats Uyghur stress as lexically contrastive in a small set of disyllabic minimal pairs (Table 1: ˈaʧa 'elder sister' vs aˈʧa 'branching', ˈbala 'child' vs baˈla 'disaster', ˈara 'fork' vs aˈra 'between' ...); 'Uyghur stress is not well understood (explanations invoke vowel length, syllable structure, and location in the stem)'; across three experiments duration, not f0 or intensity, cues stress. Note: marks 'child' as ˈbala (initial) where Nadzhip 1971:63 gives bal
sources.note: Documents lexically contrastive disyllabic minimal pairs (ˈbala 'child' vs baˈla 'disaster') and duration-only cues; bears on the record's 'strict' flag and on the empty lexical-exception/caution fields.
